text:
will: FYI — FinTrust (enterprise POC) pushed back: they won’t accept VPC peering. They want PrivateLink + an on‑prem VPN tunnel to their TGW. NetOps asked for a succinct firewall/handshake checklist and whether we require NAT in their VPC for the POC. Any recommended pattern?

maya: PrivateLink is the right initial ask if they refuse peering. Pros: no cross‑account route propagation, control on acceptor side, and minimal exposure. Cons: not transitive, ENI IPs show up in their subnet. For POC we usually do: endpoint service in our account -> customer creates interface endpoint in their VPC -> customer allows traffic to endpoint SG.

aj: Important callouts: 1) PrivateLink is not transitive across TGW — if their on‑prem goes via TGW make sure the endpoint is reachable from the TGW attachment VPC (or use a proxy). 2) We can avoid NAT in customer VPC if all required calls hit internal endpoints (endpoint service, S3 interface endpoints). But image/model bootstrap might require outbound S3/internet unless staged.

maya: Quick firewall snippet to give NetOps (they asked for copy/paste):
```
# Customer outbound allowlist (minimal)
DEST: <redwood-endpoint-ENI-IP-or-endpoint-fqdn>
PORTS: TCP 443 (HTTPS)
OPTIONAL: TCP 8443 (admin/control plane) if agreed in SOW
PROTO: TCP
NOTES: Prefer SG allow by endpoint ENI SG (if they can reference it). Avoid 0.0.0.0/0 rules.
```

will: They specifically asked "can you give us static IP ranges to allowlist?" — they need it for firewall policies.

aj: For POC we can publish a small per‑AZ ephemeral CIDR (example: 10.240.64.0/24 AZ-a, 10.240.65.0/24 AZ-b) but label as subject to change. For enterprise/contracted deployments we can provide stable ranges or allowlist by SG/cert/SNI. Recommend: allow by SG + mTLS or SNI if they want less churn.

carla: Also add these operational items to the checklist: flow logs enabled, DNS resolution for interface endpoints (they must not block AWS private DNS), and a route table entry pointing to the ENIs. If they insist on zero internet egress, call out the bootstrap caveat — we can pull model artifacts from their S3 (we can sign an S3 pull role) so nothing leaves their network.

maya: Handshake steps I normally send to customers:
1) Customer creates VPC endpoint (interface) in chosen subnets and tags it with agreed name.
2) Customer sends endpoint ID to us; we accept the endpoint service connection (one‑time).
3) Customer updates SG to allow outbound to our endpoint ENI SG (or allow to endpoint IPs).
4) Customer ensures endpoint private DNS is enabled for the service so fqdns resolve internally.
5) Confirm route tables/subnet AZs and test with a curl to the endpoint fqdn from a bastion.

will: Perfect. They also want to know cost/impact — does PrivateLink add extra egress or monthly charges?

aj: Yes there are AWS charges for interface endpoints (hourly + data processed). From our side we bill normal usage. For POC call it out as "customer will see endpoint charges + standard data transfer". For pricing discussions leave to sales, but include a short note in the checklist.

carla: Action items: I’ll draft a one‑page firewall + handshake checklist (include sample SG rules and the code block). Will book a 30m NetOps call with them Wed 10am PST. @will please confirm.

will: Confirmed — booked Wed 10am PST. I’ll attach the checklist to the invite and ask them to pre‑share their subnet CIDRs and current TGW topology. :thumbsup:

eng-bot: deploy-notice: created doc draft at /internal/sales/playbooks/fintrust-privatelink-checklist (for review).

maya: Good — also remind them to enable VPC Flow Logs for the subnets used by the ENIs so we can validate connectivity during onboarding.

will: Thanks team — sending checklist + meeting invite now.
